_comment: Windows PowerShell 5.1 compatibility baseline for the Weekly Maintenance compatibility matrix. Until 2026-09-07 that job ran `shell: pwsh` (PowerShell 7), so the 5.1 compatibility claim had never been tested. This is a regression gate, not a pass mark: CI fails if FailedCount rises above this number, and warns (without failing) if it drops, so an improvement is visible but does not break the build.
Notes: MEASUREMENT CONTRACT: this number is only comparable when produced by the exact invocation in maintenance.yml (Invoke-Pester with PesterConfiguration.psd1, CodeCoverage disabled, ExcludeTag Performance/Slow). An earlier reading of 444 came from `.pester.ps1 -CI`, a different configuration; do not mix the two.

PENDING RE-MEASUREMENT (2026-09-07): the invocation now excludes the 'Performance' and 'Slow' tags, because 'Module Performance' in ModuleLoading.Tests.ps1 asserts wall-clock load times (5s/15s) and a slow runner would redden a COMPATIBILITY gate with no code change. 456 was measured BEFORE that exclusion, so it is now a ceiling rather than an exact baseline. Excluding tests can only lower the count, so the gate stays green; the step emits a ::warning:: with the true number, which should then be recorded here.

Root cause of the failed CONTAINERS: Modules/PC-AI.LLM/PC-AI.LLM.psm1 and Modules/PC-AI.Virtualization/PC-AI.Virtualization.psm1 open with `#Requires -PSEdition Core`, so Windows PowerShell (Desktop edition) cannot load them at all, and every test file that imports them fails to load. Their manifests advertised PowerShellVersion = '5.1', a contract the modules could not honour; both manifests now declare 7.0 + CompatiblePSEditions Core.

Lowering this number is tracked work, not a CI fix. The honest options are (a) drop the Core-only requirement where the code does not actually need PS7 features, or (b) tag those suites so they are skipped under 5.1 rather than counted as failures.
The same suite under PowerShell 7 has a much smaller failure count; see commit 15f999a for that separate, pre-existing test-contract debt.
